classification.difficultyReason: Foundation: choose between two supplied displays and justify practicality. The drawing-time hint and taught comparison of column heights with keyed pictogram symbols make the essential reasoning direct.

inlines.text: The two graphs below display the same data. Explain which one is more appropriate, and why.
(Hint: how much time would it take to draw each vending machine?)

spec.description: Separated columns on an extended square grid. Category labels retain their order and the wrapped final category. Decorative red column fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Column heights 19, 23, 7, 6. Labelled vertical ticks 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24; grid continues to 28 and outside the axes. The graphical heights agree with the pictogram.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied comparison graph, visible in questions.

spec.description: Four labelled rows of editable vending-machine symbols, separated from labels by a vertical divider. Machines retain a product window, product marks and a dispensing slot. Partial symbols show the left half.
spec.mathematics: Rows contain 9.5, 11.5, 3.5 and 3 machines. With two students per machine these represent 19, 23, 7 and 6 students.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied comparison graph. The key is supplied separately immediately below.

spec.sourceRegion: Below the right-hand pictogram, aligned right
spec.description: Outlined white key with one complete vending-machine symbol.
spec.mathematics: One machine represents two students; the identical half-symbol in the pictogram therefore represents one student.

answer.short: The column graph is quicker to draw and easier to interpret.
answer.worked: The column graph shows frequencies directly through column heights. Drawing the detailed vending machines takes longer, and counting whole and half symbols takes longer than comparing the columns.
